articles.title: Baker Mayfield Gives Injury Update, Latest on Bucs QB's Status vs. Lions
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is active for Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is active for Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported earlier Sunday morning that Mayfield "is determined to play through" the injury described as "a painful case of plantar fasciitis."

Mayfield suffered a foot sprain during Tampa Bay's 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. He's still dealing with pain from the injury but was "pushing through it," according to NFL insider James Palmer .

Mayfield is "expected to wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize the foot," according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero . "He also has been dealing with the aftereffects of a dislocated right thumb suffered in Week 2 that sidelined him for three games. But he has now shed the special glove he wore for two games," added Pelissero.

Mayfield told reporters that he "felt good" during a press conference on Thursday, per Rapoport .

Mayfield said he practiced in a "limited fashion."

"Just trying to get as much as I can in," Mayfield said about his practice. "The mental side of it. Hopefully, [I can] get more tomorrow and go from there."

When asked if he felt like he could play this week, Mayfield nodded and confirmed: "I'm ready."

The 31-year-old signed a three-year, $165 million contract extension this offseason, but the early production has left a lot to be desired. Mayfield opened the 2026 season with three consecutive losses before dislocating his thumb during a 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3.

The thumb injury held him out of action for three games. After Mayfield returned, he led the Buccaneers to two crucial divisional victories over the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons — although the team didn't need him to complete a single pass in the latter contest.

The Buccaneers went into their Week 10 bye with a 3-6 record, but they can still win a division title in the NFC South despite their struggles. Although they currently trail the Panthers by one game, ESPN Analytics gives the Buccaneers a 61 percent chance of winning the division this season.

Mayfield has completed 60.6 percent of his passes for 922 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions in six games.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s early NFL days revisited as Bernard Pollard recalls ‘decapitated’ hit on Chiefs star
articles.summary: Former Kansas City Chiefs safety Bernard Pollard has recalled delivering a huge hit on Travis Kelce early in the tight end’s NFL career.
articles.body: Former Kansas City Chiefs safety Bernard Pollard has recalled delivering a huge hit on Travis Kelce early in the tight end’s NFL career. Pollard revealed that the moment became Kelce’s introduction to the physical side of professional football. The former safety also admitted that Kelce still brings up the incident during interviews. While remembering their on-field encounter, Pollard praised how much the Chiefs star has achieved since then. His comments come as the 37-year-old Kelce continues to play an important role in Kansas City’s offense during the 2026 NFL season.Bernard Pollard recalls the huge hit that gave Travis Kelce his ‘Welcome to the NFL’ momentPollard, who played safety for the Kansas City Chiefs from 2006 to 2008, discussed the incident during a recent interview with Kyle Odegard of RotoGrinders. He looked back at the early days of Kelce’s career and described how he introduced the young tight end to the kind of physical challenges he would face in the NFL.Remembering the encounter, Pollard did not hold back while describing the hit. He also revealed that Kelce has continued to mention the moment years after it happened.“I played him early in his career and I absolutely decapitated him. He still talks about that to this day when he does interviews. That was his ‘Welcome to the NFL’ moment. He knew he couldn’t just be running around like that in the NFL.”Pollard’s comments show that the incident remained a memorable part of their playing days. For Kelce, who was still finding his place in the league at the time, the experience was a reminder that defenders would not make things easy for him.However, Pollard’s recollection was not limited to the hard hit. He also spoke about the progress Kelce has made since those early years and the success he has enjoyed with Kansas City.“It’s really cool what Travis is doing. It’s been fun to see the growth he had and all the success he’s had in the National Football League. He’s been special.”Travis Kelce continues to produce for Kansas City Chiefs at 37Kelce has continued to be an important part of the Chiefs’ passing game in the 2026 season. Playing in his 14th NFL campaign, the tight end remains a trusted target for quarterback Patrick Mahomes and has led Kansas City in receiving yards through nine games.According to the Kansas City Chiefs’ official player statistics, Kelce has recorded 35 receptions for 512 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns. His average of 14.6 yards per catch has also been a strong part of his season.The veteran has contributed beyond his receiving numbers as well. He has one rushing attempt for one yard, which resulted in a touchdown. That gives him three total touchdowns this season, including his two receiving scores.At 37, Kelce continues to give the Chiefs another reliable option in their offense. His ability to make catches and gain yards has kept him involved in the team’s plans as the season moves forward.Kansas City is scheduled to face the Arizona Cardinals in its Week 11 game on Sunday, November 22. The Chiefs will host the Cardinals at 1 p.m. ET, with the game set to air on CBS. Kelce will once again be an important player to watch as Kansas City looks to add another win to its season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tom Brady's sports investment delivers an unexpected environmental victory with 19,500kg of plastic waste removed
articles.summary: Tom Brady had spent much of his career chasing trophies, but his investment in electric powerboat racing gave him another way to measure success.
articles.body: Tom Brady had spent much of his career chasing trophies, but his investment in electric powerboat racing gave him another way to measure success. His Team Brady outfit connected its performance on the water with a campaign to tackle plastic pollution. On December 17, 2025, the team received the first-ever E1 Blue Impact Championship title after its Race for Change initiative helped fund the removal of 19,500kg of plastic waste from oceans, rivers and coastlines. The achievement gave Brady's sporting venture a purpose that reached far beyond the finish line.Tom Brady's Team Brady linked racing points with ocean clean-upThe initiative followed a simple idea: every point earned by Team Brady during the 2025 E1 World Championship triggered the removal of 100kg of plastic waste through its partnership with the 4ocean Foundation. The model tied the team's results directly to an environmental cause, giving each race a second outcome beyond its position in the standings.Team Brady worked with 4ocean Foundation, OceanR, OMP and WaterAid through its Race for Change programme. The partnerships extended the campaign beyond collecting rubbish. OceanR produced the team's clothing using recycled plastic waste, helping prevent 4,112 plastic bottles from entering landfill. The team also worked with WaterAid to raise awareness about access to clean and safe drinking water.The campaign earned recognition from E1, the world's first all-electric raceboat championship. Judges assessed teams on their contributions to marine ecosystems, local communities and wider environmental awareness. Team Brady secured the Blue Impact title alongside its second E1 championship victory.Brady said the recognition mattered because the team had aimed to make a difference beyond competition.“Winning the E1 Championship for a second time this year is special, and earning the first ever Blue Impact Championship title means a lot. When we first set out to build the team with team principals Ben and Joe, our goal was to win both on and off the water – and we’ve done exactly that.“Our Race for Change platform has been a driving force for real environmental impact, and it was important to all of us that our commitment went beyond words. We wanted measurable change. I’m proud that we’re not just talking about doing good – we’re actually doing it. Seeing my team recognised for their hard work is truly inspiring.”Tom Brady's electric boat racing investment carried a wider purposeThe result also highlighted how sports teams could use competition to support causes outside their usual fan base. Team Brady's approach gave supporters a clear link between sporting performance and environmental action. It also placed sustainability at the centre of the team's identity rather than treating it as a separate campaign.The 19,500kg figure came from the team's performance-linked partnership with 4ocean, not from a claim that the racing itself removed pollution. That distinction mattered. The boats competed, earned points and helped fund clean-up operations carried out by the foundation.For Brady, the 2025 season showed that a sports investment could pursue two goals at once: winning championships and supporting measurable environmental work.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua reportedly out 4-5 months following knee surgery, will be sidelined for playoffs
articles.summary: Even if Sean McVay's team finds its way into the postseason, it won't have its top receiver, according to an ESPN report.
articles.body:
While the Los Angeles Rams try to make the most of a 2026 campaign that began with astronomical expectations, wide receiver Puka Nacua is already working toward 2027. He had MCL surgery on Tuesday, and his recovery timeline is considered to be four to five months, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Saturday night .

Based on that reported prognosis, the 25-year-old Nacua will miss the remainder of the regular season and the playoffs.

The two-time All-Pro wideout received recommendations from three doctors to undergo the procedure, per ESPN's latest report, which noted that team doctor Neal ElAttrache performed the operation.

The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries on Nov. 12 , a week before the NFL imposed its suspension. Like any player who lands on IR, Nacua had to sit out four games before he could return. By the time the suspension was announced, the length of that ban and his remaining time on IR were aligned.

While that situation understandably turned heads, it's worth noting that Nacua isn't the first player to serve a suspension while on IR.

The last year has been a head-scratching one for Nacua, who's among the best wide receivers in the sport but has run into off-field trouble.

This past offseason, news broke that a woman was suing Nacua. She alleged that, on Dec. 31, 2025, he made an antisemitic statement and later bit her on the shoulder. Nacua's attorney denied the woman's claim that he made such a comment and downplayed the biting as "horseplay."

In seven games this season, Nacua — the league's 2025 receptions leader — piled up 70 catches for 715 yards and 4 touchdowns. He also scored on the ground once for a 6-4 Rams team that's hardly had the start it envisioned this fall.

Nacua's injuries occurred on the final offensive snap of L.A.'s Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders. He's in the last year of his rookie contract.

His future in L.A. has yet to be determined, and he won't be available for the Rams in the short term. That said, the Rams are hoping to get veteran wide receiver Davante Adams back down the stretch, as they make a push for the playoffs .

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany celebrate another championship as KC Current add NWSL glory to their growing sports legacy
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current have given Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes another championship to celebrate, this time outside the NFL.
articles.body: The Kansas City Current have given Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes another championship to celebrate, this time outside the NFL. The club, co-owned by the couple, beat the Washington Spirit in Saturday night’s NWSL Championship game to claim the first title in its history. Brittany watched from Audi Field in Washington, D.C., and joined the players on the field after the final whistle. Patrick was preparing for the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 11 game against the Arizona Cardinals, but the result added a notable milestone to the family’s growing involvement in Kansas City sports.Brittany Mahomes joins KC Current's first championship celebrationBrittany’s presence at Audi Field made the ownership connection visible throughout the night. Cameras picked her out during the match, including when Vanessa DiBernardo put the Current ahead with an Olympico goal, scored directly from a corner.She arrived in a teal trench coat and red knee-high boots, echoing the team’s colours for the championship occasion. Her reaction to DiBernardo’s goal was lively, but the postgame scenes carried more weight. After the final whistle, Brittany went down to the pitch, embraced players and joined the team on stage as the celebrations continued.For Brittany, this was more than a chance to watch a team she supports lift a trophy. She is part of the ownership group behind the club, and the first championship gives that investment a landmark result. The Current have now secured the biggest prize in their history, with Brittany sharing the moment directly with the players.The 2-1 result gave the Current a clear finish to a demanding final against Washington, and made the postgame medal presentation a fitting celebration for a club reaching this point for the first time.Patrick Mahomes adds NWSL success to his sports ownership portfolioThe victory adds a different kind of achievement to the Mahomes family’s sporting story. Patrick is best known for his work with the Chiefs, while Brittany’s role with the Current gives the couple a presence in another major professional league. Their involvement goes beyond backing a local team from the stands. They co-own a club that has now delivered the biggest result in its history.Patrick’s absence in Washington was down to the Chiefs’ schedule. Kansas City was due to face the Arizona Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday afternoon, leaving him little room to attend the NWSL final. Brittany represented the family at Audi Field and joined the on-field celebration, collecting a championship medal on stage alongside the players.The win gives the couple another sporting milestone, but it also creates a new challenge for the club. The Current now have a title to defend and a standard to maintain. Whether they can turn this first NWSL crown into sustained success will be the next test. For now, Brittany got to celebrate the achievement with the team, while Patrick prepared for his own game the following day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes helped build the KC Current into a $325 million franchise, and their first NWSL championship could make it even more valuable
articles.summary: The Kansas City Current won their first NWSL championship on Saturday, beating the Washington Spirit 2-1 at Audi Field.
articles.body: The Kansas City Current won their first NWSL championship on Saturday, beating the Washington Spirit 2-1 at Audi Field. Vanessa DiBernardo scored from a corner kick, and Debinha added a late breakaway goal. The title arrives with a price tag already attached. Forbes valued the club at $325 million this year, second in the league behind Angel City. Brittany Mahomes helped found the team in December 2020, when it had no stadium and no history. Now comes the business question: does a trophy make the club worth more?How Brittany Mahomes helped build a $325 million franchiseBrittany Mahomes did not write every check, and it helps to say so plainly. Angie and Chris Long are the majority owners. Chris runs Palmer Square Capital Management, and the couple led the push to build CPKC Stadium. Brittany brought an early yes and a name people in Kansas City already knew. A former forward at UT Tyler, she joined the Longs in December 2020 as a founding co-owner, back when the club was a promise on paper.The first results were ugly. The Current finished last in the league in 2021. The owners kept building anyway. Patrick Mahomes joined the group in January 2023, the first active NFL player to own part of an NWSL team. In March 2024 the club opened CPKC Stadium, a $140 million venue financed privately and widely called the first built for a women's pro team. A $52 million training center followed.Money followed the buildings. Sportico counted $42.9 million in revenue for the Current in 2025, up from $36 million in 2024, when the club led the league. Brittany also joined the NWSL's advisory board in 2025, which gives her a voice in where the league goes next.How the KC Current beat the Spirit for their first NWSL titleA year ago, this story ended differently. The Current won the 2025 Shield in record time, then lost a playoff game to Gotham FC. Brittany posted afterward: "We'll be back. Thank you KC for the most incredible season."This year was messier. Kansas City entered the playoffs as the fourth seed under first-year coach Chris Armas. They beat Gotham 2-1 in the semifinal, with Haley Hopkins scoring in the 89th minute, then traveled to face a Spirit side playing near home.The final was rough. The Guardian reported 19 fouls in the first half, the most in any half of an NWSL final. DiBernardo broke the game open in the 54th minute with a corner that curled into the far side of the net. At 34, she became the oldest player to score in an NWSL final and was named MVP. She had her first child in January and returned in March. "This one just felt a little lighter," she said.Debinha settled it in stoppage time, rounding goalkeeper Sandy MacIver after Kansas City won the ball back. Trinity Rodman pulled one back with a header in the 98th minute, but the Spirit never found the equalizer. Washington has now lost three straight finals.Can one trophy raise a $325 million valuation?Not directly. Forbes and Sportico build their lists on revenue, recent team sales and league growth, not on trophies. Both lists also came out before this final. Forbes put the Current at $325 million, up 18% from $275 million a year earlier. Sportico had them at $315 million, with the league average at $184 million, up 77% since 2024.The trophy works through revenue. A champion sells more sponsorships, more jerseys and more media time, and it gets an earlier call when brands pick partners. Sportico's 2024 study valued NWSL clubs at about 6.8 times revenue on average. As a rough guide, and this is my own arithmetic rather than a forecast, every extra $5 million in yearly revenue would add about $34 million in value.There is also a story effect. Forbes noted that for many clubs lower in the table, valuations reflect investor bets on league growth more than current business. A championship gives buyers a better story to bet on. In a league where Denver paid a $110 million expansion fee, stories matter.Where the KC Current's growth could hit a ceilingDemand is the easy part of the argument. Room is the hard part. CPKC Stadium drew 11,500 fans for its opening match, and the club has sold out its home games, so ticket income sits close to its limit. Prices can rise. Seats cannot.That pushes the next dollars toward sponsors, media and non-matchday business, which is where a champion has leverage. Forbes also estimated that the Current could move out of the red this year. That matters in a league where, according to Sportico, every club lost money in 2024.The gap at the top is small. Angel City leads the Forbes list by $15 million, and the Spirit, who just lost the final, sit at $215 million. A title could narrow the attention gap even if Angel City stays first.Nobody can put a number on the bump today, and anyone who does is guessing. The real test comes when Forbes next updates its list, after a full offseason of sponsor talks with a championship to sell.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans scouted SMU vs. Notre Dame on Saturday
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans hold five top 65 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and scouts were spotted at the SMU versus Notre Dame game.
articles.body:
The college football season is in the home stretch heading into Week 13, and NFL scouting departments nationwide are busy evaluating talent ahead of the 2027 NFL Draft.

As you all know, the Tennessee Titans are tough to track, with their scouting department apparently using stealth technology to keep their targets hidden, and now that they would hold the first-overall selection, that is a bit frustrating.

Heading into the draft, Tennessee holds nine picks including two first-round and two second-round picks, giving them five of the top 65 selections.

The Titans have had back-to-back solid drafts and have started to lay a solid foundation. General manager Mike Borgonzi has talked about adding talent through the draft, and any added picks could speed up the process.

This week has been no different, with the Titans' scouts being less visible than those from other organizations. Here is a look at the game where Tennessee was known to have a presence.

This game does feature some intriguing prospects that could interest the Titans from both teams, including cornerback Leonard Moore, edge Boubacar Traore, offensive lineman Guerby Lambert and safety Luke Talich from Notre Dame and offensive tackle PJ Williams and tight end Theo Melin-Ohrstrom from SMU

articles.title: Do the Packers play today? Schedule, next game after bye
articles.summary: Do the Green Bay Packers play today? Here’s what to know about their schedule and games today during Week 11 of the NFL season.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packer have reached a unique portion of their 2026 schedule.

They are off in Week 11 but they won't be getting a full two weeks between games normally afforded to teams on a bye.

Matt LaFleur's Packers will already return to the field on Wednesday, Nov. 25, for the NFL's first-ever game on Thanksgiving Eve.

They'll then actually have more days off before their following game than they did during their official bye week.

Either way, the actual bye comes at a critical juncture in the season for the Packers. They're a week removed from an ugly showing in an important NFC North game at home, putting any division title hopes on life support.

The importance from here on out only intensifies if the Packers, at 6-4 through 10 games, have aspirations of reaching the playoffs for a fourth straight year.

The bye, even though it's shorter than normal, does give players banged up a few extra days to recover. And the biggest development could come with All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons, who appears poised to play in his first game in over 11 months after tearing his ACL in December 2025.

Here's what to know about the Packers' schedule, next game, Week 11 games on Sunday, NFC North standings and more:

Here are the Packers injuries during the 2026 season

No, the Packers do not play today, Nov. 22. They have a bye in Week 11.

After a 1-2 start, the Packers won five of six games to get to 6-3. But then it came crashing down again last week against the Minnesota Vikings in a 30-10 loss at Lambeau Field.

See Aaron Rodgers' and Mike McCarthy's relationship over the years

The Packers return to the field in just a matter of days when they play the Los Angeles Rams in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The Packers-Rams game kicks off the Week 12 slate and holiday schedule that includes three games on Thanksgiving and one on Black Friday.

The matchup is scheduled for 7 p.m. at SoFi Stadium.

And it's a crucial game for both squads. The Packers and Rams are each 6-4 and fighting to make a playoff push.

While the Rams have sustained major injuries to key offensive players, they have won four straight games, while Green Bay has split its last four.

Like the Packers, the Rams have a bye in Week 11 due to the rare Wednesday game in Week 12.

The NFC North is the only division in which all four teams have records above .500.

The Packers have two consecutive road games after the bye. But then they have four of their final five games of the season at Lambeau Field. The only road game in that stretch is a trip to Soldier Field to play the Chicago Bears on Christmas Day.

articles.title: ‘Expert in broken relationships’: Fans blast Dianna Russini’s take on Brandon Aiyuk’s failed NFL return
articles.summary: Dianna Russini lands in hot water with NFL fans after her latest take on Brandon Aiyuk. It has been more than two years since Brandon Aiyuk played for the Sa...
articles.body:
Dianna Russini lands in hot water with NFL fans after her latest take on Brandon Aiyuk.

It has been more than two years since Brandon Aiyuk played for the San Francisco 49ers. Initially, Aiyuk was ruled out due to a severe knee injury.

But Aiyuk still has returned to the field despite recovering from his injury due to his contract disputes with the 49ers.

NFL analyst Dianna Russini decided to share her two cents on Aiyuk's failed attempt in 2026, but her take didn't sit well with fans.

Dianna Russini reveals what's really happening between Brandon Aiyuk and San Francisco 49ers

During a recent episode of her podcast, 'The Russini Report,' the former ESPN analyst explained the real reason why Aiyuk hasn't been able to return to the 49ers, and it has nothing to do with his knee injury.

"This stopped being about a knee a long time ago. This is about money, trust, and a relationship that broke somewhere along the way. Could he still help them? Yeah, of course.

"Look at San Francisco's injury report and tell me they couldn't use him, but this is about culture. This is about a team that knows what it is, who wants, and knows what it wants to be," Russini said.

She then explained that the 49ers already have a room full of veteran leaders, including George Kittle and they simply no longer need Aiyuk in the mix before delivering the final nail in the coffin.

"So where do things stand right now? I can tell you based on talking to players and people close to the situation. This is not going to end in a reunion, and the plan is for the 49ers to release him," she concluded.

If Russini's report is correct, then there's a very high chance that Aiyuk has already played his final game with the 49ers.

Dianna Russini gets trolled by NFL fans for her Brandon Aiyuk take

However, NFL fans on X didn't seem to agree with the analyst's take and made fun of her comments instead.

"I think Russini knows a thing or two about broken relationships," a fan wrote. While another added, "She's an expert in broken relationships."

"Stop lying, stop being a fraud – you have zero credibility," a third fan stated angrily. "You had to know this post wasn't going to go well this HAD to be intentional," a fourth fan noted.

"I respect posting through it because you gotta keep it moving. Wording could be better," a fifth fan advised.

As expected, most fans made it about her alleged affair with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel and ignored what she had to say about the Aiyuk situation.

articles.title: Eagles News: ESPN predicts a Philadelphia upset
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 11/22/26.
articles.body:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Might the Philadelphia Eagles actually win a football game today?! I'm not counting on it. But I do think it's more possible after seeing the Pittsburgh Steelers drop from being 4.5-point road favorites to 3.5-point road favorites.

Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Philadelphia Eagles +4.5 (+180 moneyline) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers hasn't given much reason to trust Pittsburgh laying points on the road Sunday. Philadelphia's specialty is playing more man coverage and sending extra rushers, both of which have bothered Rodgers in 2026. Plus, defensive tackle Jalen Carter can attack an offensive line that just lost guard Mason McCormick (ankle). Eagles backup QB Joe Milton taking sacks is the main concern for their offense, but he can still get positive yards as a scrambler. With wide receiver DeVonta Smith potentially returning from a hamstring injury, the Eagles have enough to win this by a field goal.

The Eagles have been so bad this season that they've forced me to change what I write about. I really enjoy studying opposing teams for the weekly previews, but I'm already more interested in what the Eagles might look like next year. So, over the remaining weeks of the season, I'm going to examine potential coaching candidates and some offenses and defenses that interest me. Obviously, this depends on the Eagles making changes, and in this particular case, the Colts letting Shane Steichen go. Neither is guaranteed. However, I thought it would be interesting to look beyond the record and examine whether Steichen is still someone Eagles fans should want back.

The Steelers are getting one of their top wide receivers back ahead of Week 11's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Pittsburgh announced Saturday that wide receiver Roman Wilson has been activated to the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's game. In addition, the team announced the signing of edge rusher K.J. Henry from the practice squad to the roster. The two signings fill the open spots on the Steelers' roster. The Henry signing follows the Steelers announcing outside linebacker Nick Herbig as out for Sunday's game. Now, Pittsburgh has an open slot on its practice squad.

Expect to see Ty Robinson take some of the nose-tackle snaps previously reserved for Jordan Davis at the heart of the Eagles defense this season. He's an unconventional fit for the position at 6-foot-5, 288 pounds, but Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said the second-year lineman out of Nebraska has gotten extensive work in practice playing as a zero technique and believes he can hold up even with a relatively smaller frame for the role. "The nose tackle isn't totally the position that is viewed as it was in the past," Fangio said. "When there was a two back running game and there was a lot of [isolation runs] where he would get a lot, a lot of double teams. It still happens, but not as much as it used to." Robinson said it would be "big shoes" to fill in for Davis, but wasn't concerned about his size in the new role. "All last year I was learning all three positions," Robinson said. "The playbook is the easiest part now. It's just about going out there and executing and trying to fill the shoes of Jordan Davis. And those are some big shoes to fill. … It's just about the heart of the dog in the fight. I go against Jordan Mailata every day. That dude's massive. We go against massive dudes. It's nothing discouraging, just going out there and playing the way I know how to play."

Nolan Smith and Jordan Davis were teammates at Georgia and then became teammates again in the NFL. They have been friends for a long time. But there's no time to be sad. "Man, he's a great guy," Smith said on Friday. "That's part of the business. That's how it goes. I'm pretty sure Jacksonville is picking up a good player. But we have to focus on us. We have leaders in this locker room. We've got guys who can lead and push guys." Davis was traded to the Jaguars ahead of the trade deadline last week and this was the first chance to catch up with Smith since the trade. So it has been over a week since it all went down. Jalen Carter, who also played with Davis at Georgia before becoming teammates in the NFL, was again not available to reporters this week. The return on the Davis trade for the Eagles was undeniable. Getting a first-round pick and second-round pick for Davis represented incredible value. But it doesn't mean they won't miss Davis. "Man, it was special," Smith said of their time together in Philly. "But that time come and go, man. I'm still playing with guys that I played with at Georgia. But that was a real special moment, though."

Handling the Steelers' blitz game. There are individual stars here – T.J. Watt has 7.5 sacks and 9 tackles for loss – but it's the collective that makes the Steelers so good on defense. They bring pressure and they aren't afraid to expose their back end to one-on-one matchups and that's why having Smith is so critical. They can win those matchups. But the Eagles first have to handle pressure. Quarterback Joe Milton III said he has confidence in how much he worked to advance his understanding of the scheme and of what Pittsburgh does, so we will see how the Eagles react. Milton ran for 65 yards against the Giants two weeks ago. He can gash the blitz with his legs, but the Eagles also need to make the passing game go and avoid negative plays.

The Cincinnati Bengals have placed [Eagles Super Bowl LIX champion] linebacker Oren Burks on the injured reserve list with a groin injury, the team announced on Saturday. Burks, a ninth-year player, has played in all nine games this season, totaling seven tackles and one tackle for loss on defense to go with nine tackles on special teams. He suffered his injury during the team's Week 10 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Fast-forward nine games, and the Giants' secondary has been much, much, better than anticipated under [former Eagles assistant] Dennard Wilson, Donald D'Alesio, and Addison Lynch. The Giants are currently fielding the NFL's fourth-best defense in total yardage allowed (2,751 total yards). They're third-best in passing yardage allowed per game (184.1 yards per game), second in yards per completion allowed (9.8 yards per completion), and 2nd in yards per attempt allowed (6.2 yards per attempt). The Giants are accomplishing this feat with smothering coverage from their starting corners. Both Deonte Banks and Greg Newsome II have been incredibly sticky in man coverage, allowing little separation for receivers.

The Dallas Cowboys desperately need a win, and Sunday's matchup against the Tennessee Titans offers a chance to get something positive going after all the Christian Parker drama. Tennessee is 1-8 and has one of the league's worst defenses, particularly in the secondary. Dallas should have plenty of opportunities to move the ball through the air, especially with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens coming off productive performances. There are still reasons to be cautious. The Cowboys' defense has been a disaster this year, and Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward has improved over the past few weeks. With Dallas also changing its defensive play-calling, this matchup could tell us a lot about the team's direction. Here are two players to buy and one area to sell ahead of Sunday's game.

Washington's defense will be tested by the Cincinnati Bengals offense, which has scored 30-plus points in their last five games. Quarterback Joe Burrow might be this defense's kryptonite, considering how well he and the Bengals coaching staff handles the blitz. Burrow has the third-highest success rate when facing five rushers or more and has the NFL's highest completion rate at 73.4% against the blitz. Also, Jones said that Cincinnati prioritizes protection and does a good job disguising their work in pass pro. Does all that impact how Jones will call Monday night's game? He isn't volunteering that. He did provide the primary objective, to keep Burrow off balance. "We have to, in some way shape or form, provide mental stress," Jones said. "He can't be sitting back there knowing our coverage. We have to find a way to change the picture. It's going to become a chess match."

Grand Theft Auto VI is the highest-budget entertainment product in history, and if you've spent any time with the game, you'd understand why. The attention to detail is alarming; the depth of Rockstar's version of Florida is staggering — and the in-game radio has some of the most stunning celebrity DJs imaginable. One of these is comedian Stavros Halkias, who hosts a sports talk radio show that is completely off the rails. Stavros rants about bad performances by Vice City's football teams, claims that every other sport isn't manly — and even has an extended take on why Deshaun Watson did nothing wrong. Watson is never mentioned by name, but listen to this for just a few seconds and it's OBVIOUS.

articles.body: Jaylen Harrell, jugador de los Tennessee Titans, se encuentra hospitalizado después de sufrir un accidente automovilístico en Florida. "En este momento, Jaylen permanece hospitalizado y continúa recibiendo atención médica", añadieron los Titans. "Pedimos que se respete la privacidad de Jaylen y su familia. articles.body: Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce may be the most recognisable faces associated with Garage Beer, but building a national beer brand takes more than celebrity power. Behind the brothers' public appearances and promotional campaigns is a team of beverage industry professionals handling the business. Founder Andy Sauer leads the company, while executives with experience at major drinks brands oversee finance, sales and marketing. Their work reveals a different side of the Kelce brothers' business venture, one that operates well beyond the football field.Andy Sauer leads Garage Beer as Travis and Jason Kelce remain ownersSauer is the central figure in Garage Beer's management structure. The founder and CEO has guided the brand's growth and remains a significant shareholder alongside the Kelce brothers. When private investment firm Durational Capital Management backed the company in September 2025, Garage Beer confirmed that Travis, Jason and Sauer would remain operators and major shareholders.The brothers have also described themselves as active participants rather than passive investors. In their September 2025 announcement, they said: "A lot of our best memories, celebrations and conversations have come with a beer by our side," said Travis and Jason Kelce, Garage Beer shareholders and operators.However, daily operations require a wider team. Brian Amicon serves as president, while Patrick Brang joined as chief financial officer in March 2026. Brang brings experience from Founders Brewing and BeatBox Beverages. He oversees financial strategy and operations as the company expands.Andrew McGuire, meanwhile, joined as chief revenue officer after spending more than 20 years at Molson Coors. His background in sales, distributor management and national accounts gives Garage Beer experienced leadership in commercial growth.Garage Beer strengthens its marketing and production teamThe company has continued adding specialists as its reach grows. In November 2026, it appointed Justin Kelly as senior vice president of marketing. His previous experience includes roles at Liquid Death and White Claw, two brands known for distinctive marketing.Garage Beer also relies on outside partners to produce and distribute its products. It uses contract brewing rather than operating its own brewery. City Brewing in Memphis has served as its primary production partner, with Founders Brewing in Michigan providing additional capacity. The Molson Coors distributor network has also helped the brand reach customers across the United States.This structure helps explain how the Kelce brothers can remain involved while continuing their careers. articles.title: New Daniel Jones Rumors on Decision for Next Contract as NFL Landing Spots Updated
articles.summary: Veteran quarterback Daniel Jones will be patient as he weighs his next move after the Indianapolis Colts placed him on waivers.
articles.body:
Veteran quarterback Daniel Jones will be patient as he weighs his next move after the Indianapolis Colts placed him on waivers.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Jones will "wait for the right opportunity with the right team at the right time," assuming he clears waivers.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic cited the Arizona Cardinals and New England Patriots as possible landing spots given their need for a quarterback. Schefter and Rapoport also included the Baltimore Ravens, who are still without Lamar Jackson.

Interested suitors might be resolved to letting Jones hit full free agency. Taking on his current contract would carry a substantial cost for 2027.

Jones is by far the best quarterback on the market, but that says more about how few options are out there.

If the 29-year-old had been playing well, then the Colts wouldn't have cut him or would've found a satisfactory trade ahead of the deadline. Instead, they were willing to acknowledge they made an expensive mistake with his two-year, $88 million contract.

Jones has thrown for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and an NFL-high 13 interceptions. His 29.1 QBR is the worst among the 31 qualfied QBs, per ESPN.com .

As bad as those numbers are, Jones would be an upgrade for the Patriots or Cardinals.

New England is turning to Tommy DeVito as its starter after Drake Maye suffered a serious ankle injury. Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore and then watched Gardner Minshew II and Carson Beck go down with injuries. Josh Johnson will line up under center Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Patriots look like the most attractive situation for Jones. They're still in the AFC playoff race at 5-5, and he'd have a straightforward path to the starting job.

The Ravens (4-6) are further down in the standings and already acquired Brissett to stabilize their QB situation. He had 340 yards and an interception in their 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers.

Schefter and Rapoport reported the Minnesota Vikings could circle back after inquiring about Jones prior to the trade deadline. But they likewise addressed their quarterback room by reuniting with Kirk Cousins.

Depending on how long Jones wants to deliberate, a new opportunity could materialize. For now, New England is his best bet.

This decision comes days after Indianapolis waived quarterback Daniel Jones.

The Colts hit the reset button weeks ago by firing general manager Chris Ballard and then trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. More trades followed. Now, Jones is on the way out, only months after he signed a two-year, $88 million contract.

When the organization has given up on the season, there isn't much sense in having Pierce risk another injury setback given that exact situation unfolded once already. He had offseason surgery and "came back before he was fully ready," in the words of Rapoport.

The Colts have Pierce signed for three more seasons, and his salary cap hit begins climbing north of $30 million in 2027. His and the Colts' focus should be on doing everything they can to have him rebound next year.

In the meantime, the state of Indy's passing game will be dire over the final six games. Anthony Richardson Sr. is back as the starting quarterback, and Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks and Anthony Gould are his best aerial targets.

articles.title: NFL’s Jaylen Harrell hospitalised and investigated for assault in car crash
articles.summary: Police in US investigating whether Tennessee Titans defensive end assaulted rideshare driver before collision.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen ‌Harrell has been hospitalised in Florida ⁠after being ⁠involved as a passenger in a rideshare car in what the team have called a “serious” accident.

The Tampa Police Department said in ⁠a preliminary report that Harrell was riding about 8:45am (13:45 GMT) on Friday in the back seat when “he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle ⁠was in motion.”

The driver of the Kia Sorento then swerved, struck a Toyota Highlander and collided with a utility pole, the police report said.

Harrell, 24, was thrown from the backseat, hit the windshield and lost consciousness, according ‌to the police report.

Harrell was hospitalised with serious injuries while the rideshare driver, identified as a man in his mid-30s, sustained “minor injuries” and was treated at the scene, according to police. The driver of the Highlander was not injured, the police said.

Detectives are working through the timeline of events in investigating the crash, according ⁠to the preliminary report.

The Titans issued a statement ⁠on Saturday but did not disclose Harrell’s condition or the injuries he had suffered nor did they mention the assault accusation.

Harrell has not played this season after tearing ⁠an ACL in August during the preseason and being placed on the injured reserve list.

“We have been in constant communication with Jaylen’s ⁠family and are still working to gather more ⁠information,” the team said in its statement.

“At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family’s privacy be respected ‌at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate.”

The accident occurred in Tampa, Harrell’s hometown.

The Titans selected the University of Michigan alumnus in the ‌seventh ‌round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He has appeared in 34 games (two starts) and has 38 tackles, seven tackles for a loss and 4.5 sacks.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins Nears NFL History But Does QB Object 'The Unique Opportunity' After Vikings Trade?
articles.summary: After being traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings earlier this month, veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins can become the first quarterback in the modern era to play 18 regular-season games in a single year.
articles.body:
After being traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings earlier this month, veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins can become the first quarterback in the modern era to play 18 regular-season games in a single year.

While many are wondering whether the 38-year-old would prefer a week off, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Cousins "has voiced no objection to the unique opportunity to make NFL history, and he is prepared for the challenge ahead, starting with Sunday's game in Mexico City against the San Francisco 49ers."

Cousins started the first nine games of the season for the Raiders before being sent to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Since Minnesota already had its bye in Week 6 and Las Vegas' bye wasn't until Week 13, the four-time Pro Bowler could be on the field for all 18 weeks of the regular season.

The Jacksonville Jaguars also had players in the same situation when they acquired safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and defensive tackle Jordan Davis from the Philadelphia Eagles. However, the team opted to rest Bates and Davis in last week's win over the Tennessee Titans to avoid 18 straight weeks of action. Cousins, who is filling in for injured Vikings starter Kyler Murray (hamstring), may not have that luxury.

49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, who still has a relationship with Cousins from their time together with the Washington Commanders, said he recommended that his buddy take some time off, particularly for Sunday's game.

"I reminded him he hasn't had a bye week this year and he's not going to get one, so maybe he should take it that week," Shanahan said.

In addition to being the first quarterback to play in 18 regular-season games, Cousins could become the fifth player overall to achieve the feat, joining defensive lineman Leonard Williams (2023), wide receiver Mike Williams (2024), wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (2025) and defensive end Dre'Mont Jones (2025).

Cousins is no stranger to making history, as he became the first NFL quarterback to sign a fully guaranteed multi-year contract when he originally joined the Vikings in 2018. Now that he's back in Minnesota, he could add another entry to his already impressive career resume.

articles.title: Tom Jackson Dies at Age 75, Broncos Legend Became Hall of Fame Broadcaster After NFL Career
articles.summary: Former Denver Broncos linebacker and ESPN broadcaster Tom Jackson died at the age of 75.
articles.body:
Former Denver Broncos linebacker and ESPN broadcaster Tom Jackson died at the age of 75.

"The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history," the Broncos said in a statement . "An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos' first Super Bowl team that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver. Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country."

ESPN's Chris Berman, who worked alongside Jackson in the studio, said he and his colleagues "are stunned," per Jeff Legwold of ESPN:

"I'm stunned, we're stunned and you're stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown . It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week."

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell also released a statement:

Keyshawn Johnson also addressed what Jackson meant to him:

Jackson spent his entire 14-year playing career with the Broncos. He was a three-time Pro Bowler and earned All-Pro honors in 1979.

Jackson was a key piece in Denver's "Orange Crush" defense from the mid-1970s and into the '80s. That unit helped the team capture a pair of AFC titles in 1977 and 1986 before Jackson retired.

The Broncos inducted him into their Ring of Fame in 1992.

For fans of a certain age, Jackson is far more recognizable from his on-air work with ESPN. He immediately pivoted to a media career in 1987 following his retirement, and he remained with ESPN until stepping down in 2016, returning for a brief spell in 2019.

ESPN's NFL studio coverage was must-watch television for football fans as Berman, Jackson and others broke down the biggest highlights and moments.

Jackson earned a Sports Emmy for Outstanding Studio Analyst in 2009, and the Pro Football Hall of Fame honored him with the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award in 2015.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs' heartbreaking journey from sleeping in a car with his father to buying him a house after achieving NFL success
articles.summary: For Josh Jacobs, success in the NFL means far more than scoring touchdowns or earning millions.
articles.body: For Josh Jacobs, success in the NFL means far more than scoring touchdowns or earning millions. Behind the Green Bay Packers running back's achievements is a childhood filled with uncertainty, financial hardship and sacrifices that a young boy could barely understand. There was a time when a car served as his bedroom and finding a safe place to spend the night was part of his family's routine. His father, Marty Jacobs, did everything possible to protect his children, even when he had very little to offer. Years later, Josh found a way to repay that devotion, turning a painful chapter of his life into one of his family's happiest moments.Josh Jacobs' childhood struggle began with an uncertain homeGrowing up in Tulsa, Oklahoma, Josh Jacobs experienced a childhood that looked very different from the comfortable life many professional athletes enjoy today. His parents separated when he was in fourth grade, and he went to live with his father. An apartment Marty expected to move into was not ready, and temporary arrangements with relatives eventually ran out.The father and son had nowhere stable to go. For approximately two weeks, they slept inside Marty's Chevrolet Suburban while waiting for a permanent place to stay. The back seat became Josh's bed, while his father remained in the driver's seat, trying to find a safe place to park each night.For a child, the situation was difficult to understand. Josh did not initially see himself as homeless. He thought they were simply going on another drive before he fell asleep. His father, however, understood the seriousness of their circumstances.Marty stayed awake through the nights, watching over his son and making sure he was safe. Josh later recalled that whenever he woke up, his father was still awake. That memory stayed with him long after the family found more stable accommodation.The housing problems did not end with those two weeks. As the family's circumstances became more complicated, Marty also took responsibility for Josh's four siblings. The family spent months moving between hotels and temporary homes while he tried to provide for all five children.Marty Jacobs' sacrifices shaped his son's futureThe most important part of Josh's childhood story is not simply that his family struggled financially. It is how his father responded when things became difficult.Marty worked hard to keep his children together and protect them from the worst effects of their situation. He faced long working days, difficult journeys and the constant pressure of finding affordable accommodation. Even when money was tight, he tried to give his children a sense of normality.Food was not always guaranteed, and the family sometimes depended on inexpensive meals such as white rice and ramen noodles. Marty would put his children's needs before his own, making sure they had something to eat even when he had to go without.Instead of allowing financial hardship to define their household, he encouraged his children to spend time together. They sang songs, wrote poetry and enjoyed freestyle rap sessions. Those small moments helped create happy memories during a period when life offered very little certainty.Josh gradually understood what his father had endured. The man who had stayed awake to protect him was also carrying the responsibility of raising five children while struggling to provide a permanent home.When Jacobs explained his motivation in his 2019 Players' Tribune essay, he made his feelings clear: "I run for my pops, the man who sacrificed so much and worked so hard to provide for me and educate me."That statement offered a glimpse into the personal motivation behind his football career. For Jacobs, reaching the NFL was never just about individual recognition. It was also about honouring the person who had stood beside him when success seemed far away.Josh Jacobs turned his difficult past into an NFL careerFootball gradually became an important escape from the difficulties surrounding Josh Jacobs. It gave him somewhere to focus his energy and a chance to imagine a different future.However, reaching professional football was not an easy journey. His background did not guarantee him a place among the country's top prospects. He had to work his way through high school and college, proving his ability at every stage.His time at the University of Alabama helped him take the next major step. Playing under Nick Saban, Jacobs developed into a talented running back and attracted attention ahead of the 2019 NFL Draft.The Oakland Raiders selected him with the 24th overall pick, turning years of hard work into a professional opportunity. His rookie campaign further established his value. Jacobs recorded 1,150 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns in 13 games during the 2019 regular season.Yet the numbers did not tell the entire story. For someone who had once slept in a car without knowing where he would wake up the next morning, having a professional career and financial security represented something much bigger.He had reached a position where he could offer his family the stability that had been missing during his childhood. More importantly, he could finally do something for the father who had spent years putting his children's needs first.Josh Jacobs' emotional house gift to his father completed the journeyOne of the most meaningful moments of Jacobs' early NFL career came after his impressive rookie season. Rather than celebrating his success only through personal purchases, he decided to make a major gesture for Marty.In January 2020, Jacobs surprised his father by buying him a house in Stillwater, Oklahoma. He shared the news on social media with a simple message: "Blessed just bought my pops a house."The gesture carried a meaning that went far beyond the value of the property. Marty had once searched for safe places to park their Suburban so his son could sleep. He had spent nights awake, worrying about his children's safety and trying to make sure they had a roof over their heads.Now, his son was giving him something he had struggled for years to secure: a permanent home.The surprise also represented a reversal of roles. As a child, Josh had depended on his father for protection and security. After reaching the NFL, he finally had the means to provide that same sense of comfort in return.Jacobs' journey also offers a reminder that success does not erase difficult memories. His childhood experiences remained part of his identity, influencing the way he viewed money, family and opportunity.For fans, his story is about much more than an NFL running back overcoming homelessness. It is about a father who refused to give up when circumstances became difficult and a son who remembered every sacrifice.Marty once gave his children a reason to feel safe when he had almost nothing. Years later, Josh gave him a home of his own. That may be one of the most meaningful achievements of his football career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tom Jackson dies at 75: How the Denver Broncos legend built a legacy beyond the football field
articles.summary: Tom Jackson, the Broncos linebacker who went on to become one of ESPN's most trusted voices, died at 75. His family informed the network.
articles.body: Tom Jackson, the Broncos linebacker who went on to become one of ESPN's most trusted voices, died at 75. His family informed the network. Jackson spent all 14 of his NFL seasons in Denver, started for the 1977 Super Bowl team and later worked 29 years on ESPN's studio shows beside Chris Berman. His 191 games were a Broncos record when he retired. The team and the network released statements Sunday, and Berman said he and his colleagues were stunned. The Broncos said Jackson had been part of their family for more than 50 years.Tom Jackson made his name as the Broncos' emotional leaderDenver drafted Jackson in the fourth round in 1973 out of Louisville, and he never wore another NFL uniform. He started 177 of his 191 regular-season games and played in 10 playoff games. For 11 straight seasons he ranked among the team's top five tacklers. His best year was 1980, when he made 180 stops.He could take the ball away, too. Jackson's 20 interceptions are tied with Randy Gradishar for the most by a linebacker in team history, and his seven picks in 1976 still stand as the best single season by a Broncos linebacker.Joe Collier, the defensive coordinator whose 3-4 scheme gave rise to the Orange Crush, called Jackson the emotional leader of that group. The numbers only tell part of it. Denver reached its first Super Bowl after the 1977 season with Jackson starting, the first of the franchise's eight trips. He made three Pro Bowls and went into the team's Ring of Fame in 1992.Jackson retired after the 1986 season at 36, the oldest linebacker in the league. He made it official after the 1987 draft and said the choice had nothing to do with whether he could still play. It was just time.How Jackson became a Sunday fixture at ESPNJackson went straight from the field to the studio in 1987 and stayed at ESPN until 2016. His final assignment was the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony that year. Most of his airtime came next to Berman on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown, and the network later named its NFL studio the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio.ESPN calls that distinction unmatched in its history. Chairman Jimmy Pitaro said Jackson brought the credibility of an All-Pro player and a warmth that connected with generations of fans.Jackson won a Sports Emmy for outstanding studio analyst in 2009, and the Hall of Fame gave him the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award in 2015, five years after Berman received it. He came back for a digital-only NFL Primetime in 2019, one more run with his old partner.Berman said he worked beside Jackson for 30 years and called him his best friend, both professionally and personally. Anyone who met him, Berman added, or just watched him on ESPN felt the same. Jackson often said he had been "blessed to work for two companies in my life: the Denver Broncos and ESPN."Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and daughters Taylor and Morgan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and Hall of Fame broadcaster at ESPN, dies at 75
articles.summary: Tom Jackson, a former NFL linebacker and Hall of Fame broadcaster, has died at the age of 75.
articles.body: Tom Jackson, a former NFL linebacker and Hall of Fame broadcaster, has died at the age of 75. His longtime employer ESPN announced his death on Sunday, after his family informed the network on Friday. Jackson was a fourth-round pick by the Broncos in the 1973 draft out of Louisville; Jackson played in 191 regular-season games, including 177 starts as a member of Denver’s “Orange Crush” defense. He was a three-time Pro Bowl selection and a two-time AP All-Pro. After his retirement from football in 1986, he joined ESPN where he spent 29 years and was most well-known for his role alongside Chris Berman. Berman said Jackson’s death was “unexpected” on Sunday and added that he spoke to him “at length” last week after he made a surprise appearance at the studio. “He was a vital 75,” an emotional Berman said on ESPN’s “Sunday NFL Countdown.” “Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock.” In a statement released by ESPN, Berman said that Jackson was “one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet.” “All of us are stunned,” Berman said in his statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.” ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro called Jackson “one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN’s history.” “He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans,” Pitaro said in a statement. “Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends. In fact, ESPN’s NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio, a distinction unmatched in our history and a fitting tribute to their lasting impact. “Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure.” Jackson was awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television award by the Hall of Fame in 2015 and retired from ESPN a year later after covering the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony. “Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst,” Berman continued in his statement. “There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable. He is easily summed up by this classic old song: ‘He’s got sunshine on a cloudy day.’” Jackson is survived by his wife Jen and his daughters Taylor and Morgan. “Our hearts bleed for them. We thank them for lending Tom to us. Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend too,” Berman said. This story has been updated with additional information.

articles.summary: After losing star receiver Puka Nacua to season-ending knee surgery, the Los Angeles Rams are reportedly set to get their other star wideout back in the lineup.
articles.body:
After losing star receiver Puka Nacua to season-ending knee surgery, the Los Angeles Rams are reportedly set to get their other star wideout back in the lineup.

On Sunday's episode of NFL GameDay , NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Rams veteran receiver Davante Adams had an "outside chance" to return from injured reserve for Wednesday's matchup against the Green Bay Packers, but that is "not gonna happen," and he is more likely to be activated around mid-December.

Adams underwent a procedure to repair a ruptured hamstring suffered in the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6. He was initially given a return timeline of six to 10 weeks .

Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters earlier this month that the team opted not to acquire a wide receiver at the trade deadline because he was "optimistic" that Adams would return from his hamstring injury "sooner than later." Nacua hadn't been ruled out for the season at the time, but in retrospect, the team would've benefited from another addition.

Rapoport reported that Nacua "was trying to get back from a significant MCL injury," but "was not able to do it without surgery." He underwent surgery on his MCL on Tuesday, but his PCL and turf toe were "untouched." The 25-year-old is facing a "four- to five-month recovery," ruling him out for the entire year even if the Rams advance to the Super Bowl. The 2026 season is the final year of his rookie contract, and his future in Los Angeles now appears uncertain.

The Rams are riding a four-game win streak into Wednesday's game against the Packers, and they will try to sustain their momentum until they can get Adams back onto the field.

"All of us are stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet," Berman said. "I was fortunate, as you know, to work side-by-side with him for 30 years on 'NFL Primetime' and 'NFL Gameday,' now 'Sunday NFL Countdown.'"

"Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst," he added. "There was nobody kinder, there was nobody more thoughtful, more loyal, more engaging than Tom Jackson."

Jackson died on Friday, according to Berman. His family informed ESPN of his death soon thereafter.

Jackson is known to generations of NFL fans for his work providing commentary on highlights for ESPN with Berman, long before pro football studio shows like "NFL Live" and the NFL Network became ubiquitous.

Watching clips of the day's games was never more electric than when the two detailed the action on screen with ESPN's iconic background music playing behind them during "NFL Primetime."

One of Jackson's signature bits was showing the week's hardest hits on Monday night, saying players got "Jacked Up!" Though that segment was eventually phased out as concern and consideration for head trauma and serious injury grew, Jackson conveyed the excitement and thrill that so many fans felt while watching the NFL.

Before going into broadcasting, Jackson was a linebacker for the Denver Broncos for 14 seasons. He played on two Super Bowl teams in 1977 and 1986, and ranks fourth in team history with 191 games played .

Denver's 1975 fourth-round pick out of Louisville, Jackson was named to three Pro Bowls and twice earned All-Pro honors. The Broncos inducted Jackson into their Ring of Fame in 1992.

At Louisville, Jackson played for fellow former ESPN analyst Lee Corso from 1970-72. The Cardinals also paid tribute to Jackson, who led the team in tackles in each of his three seasons. He was named the Missouri Valley Conference player of the year twice during his college career. Louisville honored his jersey No. 50 in 1999.

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said Jackson "brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did."

"The NFL lost a wonderful man with the passing of Tom Jackson," Goodell said in a statement. "Along with millions of fans, I will always remember him as a player and broadcaster, but also as a friend. He was an outstanding player whose toughness and leadership helped define an era of Broncos football. He brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did, and generations of fans came to know him through his work at ESPN. Tom helped fans enjoy and better understand football, always bringing the perspective of someone who loved the game and the people who play it. More importantly, he earned the respect and friendship of players, coaches and everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him."

articles.title: Tom Jackson, Broncos star and ESPN ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ analyst, dead at 75
articles.summary: Tom Jackson, a fiery cornerstone of the Orange Crush defense with the Denver Broncos who went on to even more fame as a beloved broadcaster on ESPN, has died, his family and the network announced Sunday.
articles.body: Tom Jackson, a fiery cornerstone of the Orange Crush defense with the Denver Broncos who went on to even more fame as a beloved broadcaster on ESPN, has died, his family and the network announced Sunday. He was 75. Jackson’s family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wishes that his death not be announced until the start of the network’s “Sunday NFL Countdown” show by Jackson’s longtime friend and on-air partner Chris Berman. A cause of death was not given. “Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable,” Berman said. “Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend, too.” Berman said Jackson made a surprise visit a couple of weeks ago to ESPN, where he worked for 32 years over two stints after playing 14 seasons for the Broncos, and that the two talked on Tuesday. A fourth-round draft pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson was an inspirational leader of Denver’s first Super Bowl team in 1977. He started 177 games for the Broncos between 1973-86, retiring after the team’s second Super Bowl appearance. He was a first-team All-Pro in 1977 and a second-team All-Pro the following season; he also was a three-time Pro Bowler. Following his playing days, Jackson had a second career at ESPN from 1987-2016 and was featured on “Sunday NFL Countdown” and “NFL Primetime.” Before the internet and NBC took over the Sunday night package in 2006, “NFL Primetime” was must-see viewing for fans and players because it showed highlights from all the games, as well as the interaction between Berman and Jackson, who often finished each other’s sentences. “I can remember coming from games and waiting in a rush to get home, to watch ‘Primetime’ because all I wanted to know was, what were you and Tom Jackson gonna say about one, the team?” ESPN analyst and Hall of Fame wide receiver Randy Moss said to Berman. Jackson briefly returned to ESPN in 2019 and reunited with Berman to do an online version of “NFL Primetime.” He was awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015. “In my lifetime there was Howard Cosell doing ‘Monday Night Football’ halftime highlights and then there were Boomer and TJ doing ‘Sunday NFL Countdown.’ I am not here as a colleague but as one of million who watched, learned from and idolized the two of you,” ESPN host Mike Greenberg said during Sunday’s show. ESPN’s studio crew wore orange ties in honor of Jackson during the three-hour show. Berman said Jackson was the last of seven people interviewed for the studio analyst job and that the last person rarely gets the job. But Jackson nailed the interview. “Tom Jackson was one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN’s history. He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans. Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends,” ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said in a statement. “Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. ... His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure.” ESPN’s NFL studio in Bristol, Connecticut, is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio. It is the only named studio on ESPN’s campus. “The Denver Broncos are heartbroken by the passing of Ring of Fame linebacker Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the legendary Orange Crush defense and one of the most beloved players in franchise history,” the Broncos said in a statement. “An inspirational leader and fierce competitor, TJ was a proud member of the Broncos’ first Super Bowl team that helped establish a winning tradition in Denver. Off the field, Tom carried himself with class, warmth and humility, forging deep connections and lifelong friendships with teammates and throughout Broncos Country.” Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and daughters Taylor and Morgan.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb Makes Cowboys History with Rare Stats as Star WR Breaks Franchise Record on Video
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys star receiver CeeDee Lamb entered a new echelon in the franchise's storied history.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys star receiver CeeDee Lamb entered a new echelon in the franchise's storied history.

Lamb caught a nine-yard pass in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans, surpassing the 1,000-yard mark this season. The team announced that he's now the first Cowboys player ever to achieve six straight seasons with at least 1,000 receiving yards.

The only time Lamb didn't reach the 1,000-yard mark was his rookie year, in which he posted 935 yards. He entered Sunday's game with 77 catches for 976 yards and eight touchdowns through his first 10 outings. He was limited to 14 games in 2025 and finished with 1,077 yards, and he's already on the verge of surpassing that total in Week 11.

Since entering the NFL as the No. 17 pick in the 2020 draft, Lamb has established himself as one of the best weapons in the game. He's been selected to each of the last five Pro Bowls, earning All-Pro honors three times in that span, including one first-team selection.

Despite Lamb's individual brilliance this year, the Cowboys have endured a rollercoaster season. Dallas entered Sunday's game against Tennessee with a 4-6 record following last week's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Any further missteps could put the team in danger of missing the playoffs for a third straight year.

The Cowboys will continue leaning on Lamb as they try to climb back up the standings and compete for a postseason spot in the NFC.

articles.title: Josh Allen, James Cook Make NFL History with Rare Rushing Stat Amid Bills QB's MVP Push
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills stars Josh Allen and James Cook III carved out a special place in NFL history during Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills stars Josh Allen and James Cook III carved out a special place in NFL history during Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.

Cook scored his 10th rushing touchdown of the season in the second quarter. He and Allen are now the first teammates to each have 10-plus touchdowns on the ground across three straight years.

With 36 rushing yards in the first half, Cook is over 1,000 total for the fourth consecutive season.

Allen, meanwhile, is dealing a small blow to his MVP campaign. He has thrown for 193 yards and one touchdown, though he does have two interceptions.

For now, the award is a four-man race. Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is the favorite (+100) at FanDuel Sportsbook and followed by Allen (+350), San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (+450) and Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (+550). Don't write off the Kansas City Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes at +2500, either.

During their last spell of sustained success, the Bills were powered by an offense that featured three Hall of Famers: Jim Kelly, Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed.

Cook still has a ways to go to catch Thomas, who's Buffalo's all-time leading rusher with 11,938 yards. Still, his consistency shouldn't be overlooked.

Cook and Allen's combined efforts are reminiscent of those great Bills teams from the 1990s.
