articles.title: Series of Ravens miscues including fumble through end zone results in 14-point swing in favor of Panthers
articles.summary: The Ravens got seven points right back with a kickoff return for a touchdown in a wild sequence of events in Charlotte.
articles.body:
Justice Hill thought he had a touchdown Sunday against the Carolina Panthers.

Instead, the Baltimore Ravens running back fumbled through the end zone to spark a wild sequence of events that ultimately resulted in a score for the Panthers.

With 12:17 remaining in the second quarter, Hill took a handoff from the Carolina 37-yard line and broke free through the secondary toward the end zone. But just before he reached the end zone, Carolina cornerback Will Lee punched the ball out of of Hill's grasp.

The ball then bounced through the end zone to trigger perhaps the most controversial rule in football. Even though the Panthers didn't recover the loose ball, they took over possession via a touchback.

Just like that, a would-be Ravens score turned into a turnover at the last moment thanks to a heads-up play from Lee.

The Panthers didn't initially do much with their good fortune. They punted after a 3-and-out on their ensuing possession. But another Ravens miscue set them up with another opportunity.

This time, LaJohntay Wester muffed the punt return, allowing the Panthers to recover deep in Baltimore territory.

And this time, the Panthers capitalized. Two plays later, Chuba Hubbard ran 18 yards around the left edge for a touchdown and a 14-12 Carolina lead.

But all was not lost for the Ravens in the wild sequence.

The very next touch for the Ravens resulted in a score. Devontez Walker returned the ensuing kickoff 86 yards for a touchdown to put the Ravens back on top with a 19-14 lead.

If you're counting, that's three consecutive Ravens touches that resulted in a fumble through the end zone, a muffed punt that led to a Carolina touchdown and a kickoff return for a Baltimore touchdown.

It was quite an eventful few minutes, and fans in Charlotte got their money's worth before halftime.

articles.title: Tom Brady Campaigns for Belichick & Kraft in New Video After Controversial Snubs for Hall of Fame
articles.summary: Legendary quarterback Tom Brady's loyalty to the New England Patriots still runs deep, and he advocated for two of the team's most important figures to be voted into the Hall of Fame.
articles.body:
Legendary quarterback Tom Brady's loyalty to the New England Patriots still runs deep, and he advocated for two of the team's most important figures to be voted into the Hall of Fame.

During Fox NFL Sunday , Brady spoke up for Patriots owner Robert Kraft and former head coach Bill Belichick to get the nod after they both were left out of the Hall of Fame last year.

"All the voters seem like they need to come to their senses on this one. These guys were architects of what a two-decade dynasty was all about," Brady said. "So, excited for everybody who's a part of that. R.K.K., what he's done for this league has just been exceptional. Bill, come on, there's nobody that I'd rather play for than him. So I'm expecting August in Canton to be a big Patriots party, that's for sure."

In addition to Kraft and Belichick, former Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski is also a Hall of Fame finalist in his first year of eligibility. If Brady has his way, all of them will be inducted together to create a special celebration for New England fans.

Three of the five finalists among contributors, coaches and senior players will need at least 40 votes for one to three nominees to be inducted alongside three to five modern era players from a group of 15 finalists. The new class of Hall of Famers will be announced in early 2027.

articles.title: Eagles QB Joe Milton III just stands and watches his fumble in shades of infamous Cam Newton Super Bowl play
articles.summary: This is not the kind of effort to get Eagles fans on your side.
articles.body:
This is not the kind of effort to get Eagles fans on your side.

Philadelphia quarterback Joe Milton III made his second start for the Eagles Sunday in place of the benched Tanner McKee and sidelined starter Jalen Hurts. He did not do his best to make a good early impression on the home fans.

On Philadelphia's second play from scrimmage, Milton was stripped of the ball in the backfield by Steelers pass rusher Alex Highsmith. But it wasn't the fumble that's likely to draw the ire of Eagles fans. It was his response to the loose ball.

Milton wasn't tackled on the play. And as the ball hit the ground near his feet, he just stood there and looked at it.

Milton made no effort to secure the loose ball that he had a chance at recovering.

Fortunately for the Eagles, left tackle Jordan Mailata did make a play on the ball and was able to secure it before Highsmith could. It was a good break for the Eagles that could go a long way in saving Milton from heat in Philadelphia.

The Eagles were able to convert the recovery into an early 3-0 lead.

The play drew immediate visions of Cam Newton. The former Carolina Panthers great made — or didn't make — a famously familiar play with considerably higher stakes attached.

With his Panthers trailing the Denver Broncos by six points in the fourth quarter of Super Bowl 50, Newton was stripped of the ball by Broncos pass rusher Von Miller.

Like Milton on Sunday, Newton had a shot at recovering the ball and made no effort to do so. But Newton's Panthers weren't as fortunate as the Eagles on Sunday.

The Broncos recovered Newton's fumble deep in Carolina territory to help seal a 24-10 Denver win.

Milton's lack of effort clearly won't go down in infamy like Newton's. But it's never a good sign to draw those comparisons.

articles.summary: During the Fox Sports' pregame show on Sunday, Tom Brady poked a little fun at Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw for siding with a division rival.
articles.body:
During the Fox Sports' pregame show on Sunday, Tom Brady poked a little fun at Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw for siding with a division rival.

"If I picked a quarterback today, I'd pick [Cincinnati Bengals quarterback] Joe Burrow," Bradshaw said to Brady. "That's me. In your opinion, what do you think makes him so special?"

"T.B., you said Joe Burrow — that's who you're picking?" Brady responded. "I'm sure the Steelers fans actually are thrilled to hear that Burrow's your quarterback you're taking. Who's second favorite, Lamar [Jackson]?

Brady's comments were a playful jab at Bradshaw, who spent his entire 14-year career with the Steelers and helped lead them to four Super Bowl championships.

Despite Bradshaw's allegiances, his admiration of Burrow isn't difficult to understand. Burrow, who plays for Pittsburgh's AFC North rival Cincinnati Bengals, is having an MVP-caliber season. He entered Sunday leading the league in completions (254), completion percentage (74.7) and passing touchdowns (27).

articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf had more costly penalties on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field than receptions.

Metcalf was ejected after the second of those infractions late in the third quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles. The final straw was when he was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct.

He was called for taunting in the wake of his latest dustup with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean. And, so, Metcalf, who was notably suspended two games last season for swinging at a Detroit Lions fan during a sideline altercation , was disqualified, with Philly fans waving goodbye to him as he walked to the tunnel.

That penalty backed up a Chris Boswell field-goal attempt, which ended up being from 52 yards out. Fortunately for Pittsburgh, Boswell still made the kick to cut the team's deficit to 16-9.
